page: The Vultr voc-s-16c-128gb-2560s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC architecture. It provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at an operating base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2 instructions. The instance does not include a discrete GPU accelerator, relying entirely on the central processor for computational tasks.

Hardware resource allocation features 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provisioned via an integrated 2560 GB NVMe SSD, delivering high-capacity on-instance non-volatile storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address. In benchmark evaluations, the memory subsystem demonstrates high throughput, achieving a top 10% result in large-block uncached memory write bandwidth at 170.21 GB/sec and a top 25% result in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth at 339.94 GB/sec.

General computing and database performance benchmarks register balanced output across common enterprise workloads. Stress-ng single-core processing scores within the top 25% at 2927.78, while multi-core processing, Geekbench multi-core (12675.0), and PassMark CPU (37081.08) metrics align with median cross-industry figures. The system handles Redis SET operations at 36.59 million operations per second and static web throughput at 15.75 GB/sec. Given its extensive NVMe storage capacity and high memory allocation per vCPU, this instance offers efficient resource density for relational databases, Redis caching layers, memory-intensive data analytics, and general-purpose backend services requiring sustained local I/O performance.

Memory subsystem performance ranks in the top tier for large-block write bandwidth (170.21 GB/sec) and top quartile for read bandwidth (339.94 GB/sec), while multi-core compute and PassMark CPU metrics sit comfortably within standard benchmark averages. Given its high RAM-to-vCPU ratio and high-capacity bundled NVMe storage, this server delivers balanced cost efficiency for database operations, caching services like Redis, memory-intensive analytics, and I/O-heavy production workloads.
